cues.en: My name is Jack Shostak. I'm a professor of genetics at Harvard Medical School. I'm an investigator at Massachusetts General Hospital, where my labs are, and I'm also an investigator of the Howard Hughes Medical Institute. In this lecture, what I'd like to tell you about is recent advances in work from my lab on the origin of cellular life on the early Earth.
cues.zh: 我是 Jack Shostak，哈佛医学院的遗传学教授。我的实验室位于马萨诸塞州总医院，同时我也是霍华德·休斯医学研究所的研究员。在这次演讲中，我想向大家介绍我们实验室在早期地球细胞生命起源研究方面的最新进展。

cues.en: But before I get into those experiments, I'd like to step back from the origin of life, per se, and talk a little bit about some insights from modern biology that bear on this question, and in particular, why the question has attracted so much interest and attention recently. So, this is one of the iconic images of hydrothermal deep sea vents.
cues.zh: 但在深入探讨这些实验之前，我想先跳出“生命起源”本身，聊聊现代生物学为这一问题带来的一些启示，特别是为什么这个问题最近引起了如此广泛的兴趣和关注。大家看到的是深海热泉喷口的标志性图像之一。

cues.en: This is an environment characterized by very high temperature and pressure, and yet, of course, the surrounding area is just teeming with life. Here's another example in an image from Norm Pace. You can see a layer of green cells growing inside the rock. These are photosynthetic cyanobacteria, and they're living in the...
cues.zh: 这里的环境具有极高的温度和压力，但即便如此，周围区域依然生机勃勃。这是来自 Norm Pace 的另一张示例图片，可以看到一层绿色细胞生长在岩石内部。这些是进行光合作用的蓝藻，它们生活在……

cues.en: pores of the rock at very low pH. This is one of the famous hot springs in Yellowstone National Park. Again, a very high temperature environment. Again, full of life. And here's yet another distinct kind of extreme environment, another very low pH environment. This is the Rio Tinto in Spain.
cues.zh: 岩石的孔隙中，处于极低的 pH 值环境下。这是黄石国家公园著名的温泉之一，同样是极高温的环境，同样充满着生命。这里还有另一种截然不同的极端环境，也是强酸性环境——这是西班牙的 Rio Tinto。

cues.en: very acidic water, but again, teeming with life, microbial, eukaryotic life. There are even more extreme examples of this kind of environment in acid mine drainage sites, where the water that's flowing out is basically sulfuric acid at a pH close to zero, and again, there's microbial life.
cues.zh: 水质酸性极强，但同样充满了生命，包括微生物和真核生物。在酸性矿山废水中，这类环境甚至更加极端，流出的水基本上是 pH 值接近于零的硫酸，但依然有微生物存活。

cues.en: So with all of these examples, what it's telling us is just the remarkable extent to which our planet has been colonized by life, and even environments that we would have considered incredibly hostile and extreme are apparently easily adapted to by life. And of course, this is a consequence of the power of Darwinian evolution
cues.zh: 所有这些例子都向我们表明，生命在地球上的繁衍范围是多么惊人，哪怕是我们认为极其恶劣严酷的环境，生命显然也能轻松适应。当然，这要归功于达尔文进化论的力量，

cues.en: to lead to adaptations to diverse environments. So if you put this together with recent observations from our astronomy colleagues in terms of the discovery of extrasolar planets, it really puts into focus the question of, you know, whether there is life out there apart from our planet. So this is an image of the Milky Way.
cues.zh: 它驱动生命去适应多样化的环境。如果把这一点与天文学界同行最近在系外行星发现方面的观测结合起来，就会让我们真正聚焦于一个问题：除了我们地球之外，宇宙中是否存在其他生命？这是一张银河系的图像。

cues.en: Of course. Up to a couple of years ago, astronomers had discovered on the order of 500 extrasolar planets, planets orbiting other stars. But more recently, as a result of the Kepler mission, a space telescope that is just pointed continuously at a very dense star field.
cues.zh: 当然，直到几年前，天文学家发现的系外行星（即围绕其他恒星运行的行星）大约有 500 颗。但最近，得益于 Kepler 任务——这是一台持续对准密集星场的太空望远镜。

cues.en: a large number of additional planets have been found, about 1,200 candidates of the last count. And these are detected as the planets orbit around their star, and if they eclipse the star, if they transit in front of it, they block out some of the light, and you can detect that little dip in the intensity of the light. So this has given us a big enough sample to actually make extrapolations.
cues.zh: 已经发现了大量额外行星，最近一次统计约有1200颗候选行星。这些行星是通过其绕恒星运行被探测到的；如果它们遮住恒星，也就是从恒星前方经过，就会挡住一部分光，你就能探测到光强的小幅下降。因此，这给了我们足够大的样本来做外推。

cues.en: What I've heard from scientists associated with the Kepler mission is that those extrapolations suggest that there could be roughly on the order of 500 million, perhaps even a billion, Earth-like planets orbiting Sun-like stars out there in our galaxy. And so, if you put that together with the fact that we know on our planet
cues.zh: 我从参与 Kepler 任务的科学家那里听到的是，这些外推表明，在我们银河系中，可能有大约5亿颗、甚至也许10亿颗类地行星绕着类太阳恒星运行。所以，如果把这一点与我们知道在我们星球上——

cues.en: that at least microbial life can live in incredibly harsh and diverse environments, it's pretty clear that there will be environments out there on these other planets that could support life. So the question is, and the thing we all really want to know, is, is there life out there? Are we alone, or is the universe, is our galaxy full of life? So this really comes down to the question you see here.
cues.zh: 至少微生物生命能够生活在极其严酷且多样的环境中，那么很清楚，这些其他行星上会存在能够支持生命的环境。所以问题是，也是我们都真正想知道的：外面有生命吗？我们是孤独的，还是宇宙、我们的银河系充满了生命？所以这真的归结为你在这里看到的这个问题。

cues.en: Is it easy or hard for life to emerge from the chemistry of early planets? And unfortunately it's going to be a long time before we can answer that question in the most satisfying way by direct observation. Even to get indirect evidence from a spectroscopy of planetary atmospheres may take 10, 20, 50 years to look at Earth-like planets.
cues.zh: 生命从早期行星的化学中产生，是容易还是困难？不幸的是，要过很长时间，我们才能通过直接观测以最令人满意的方式回答这个问题。即使要从行星大气光谱中获得间接证据，也可能需要10年、20年、50年去观测类地行星。

cues.en: So what can we do in the meantime to try to get some clues to answer this question? So what we've been doing and other people have been doing is to go into the lab and do simple chemical experiments and try to work out a complete step-by-step plausible pathway all the way from simple chemistry to more complex chemistry to simple biology.
cues.zh: 那么在此期间，我们能做些什么来尝试获得一些线索回答这个问题？所以我们一直在做、其他人也一直在做的，就是走进实验室，做简单的化学实验，试图梳理出一条完整的、逐步的、可信的路径，从简单化学一直到更复杂的化学，再到简单生物学。

cues.en: And if we can actually show that there's a continuous pathway with no super hard steps along the way, then I think we could conclude that it's likely that there is abundant life out there in our galaxy. On the other hand, it could be that our experiments show that there are some steps in that pathway that are extremely difficult.
cues.zh: 如果我们真的能证明存在一条连续路径，沿途没有特别困难的步骤，那么我想我们可以得出结论：我们银河系中很可能存在大量生命。另一方面，也可能我们的实验表明，这条路径中有一些步骤极其困难。

cues.en: they're bottlenecks that might be very hard to overcome, in which case the emergence of life might actually be a very rare phenomenon. And in the extreme, we could be it. This could be the only place in our galaxy or even the universe where life has emerged. So, we would like to try to get some insight into these questions by doing simple laboratory experiments. Now, there's a related question.
cues.zh: 它们是可能很难克服的瓶颈，在这种情况下，生命的出现也许实际上是非常罕见的现象。而在极端情况下，可能就是我们。这可能是我们银河系、甚至宇宙中唯一出现生命的地方。所以，我们想通过做简单的实验室实验，来尝试对这些问题的获得一些洞察。现在，还有一个相关问题。

cues.en: which is shown down here, if there is life out there, is it likely to be pretty similar to what we're familiar with on our planet? Will life that evolved independently elsewhere have the same fundamental kind of biochemistry? Will there be cells that are living in water, using...
cues.zh: 正如这里所展示的，如果地外真有生命存在，它会和我们地球上熟悉的生命很相似吗？在其他地方独立演化出的生命，是否会拥有相同的基础生化机制？会不会也是生活在水中的细胞，并利用……

cues.en: If not RNA and DNA, some nucleic acid to mediate heredity, will they use protein-like molecules to carry out biochemical functions? Or could there be forms of life that are actually much different, much more diverse, maybe using completely different kinds of molecules to mediate heredity and to mediate function?
cues.zh: 即便不是 RNA 和 DNA，也是某种核酸来传递遗传信息？它们会使用类似蛋白质的分子来行使生化功能吗？抑或可能存在截然不同、更为多样的生命形态，或许利用完全不同的分子来传递遗传信息和实现生理功能？

cues.en: or even forms of life that live in very different environments, for example, in solvents other than water. Again, this is the kind of thing that I think we can address by going into the lab and doing simple experiments and trying to build structures and assess the possibility of having living systems in different kinds of environments and with different molecular bases.
cues.zh: 甚至可能存在生活在极不相同的环境中的生命，比如存在于水以外的溶剂中。同样，我认为这类问题可以通过走进实验室、做些简单实验来探索，尝试构建结构，并评估在不同环境及不同分子基础下存在生命系统的可能性。

cues.en: Okay, so let's try to think then about how we can deduce something about early forms of life. After all, if we want to experimentally investigate the beginnings of life, we have to have some idea, some kind of conceptual model of what very primitive forms of life looked like. And this has been a very difficult thing for people to think about.
cues.zh: 好，那我们试着想想，该如何推测早期生命形态的样貌。毕竟，如果我们想通过实验研究生命的起源，就必须对极其原始的生命形态有一些概念，构建某种概念模型。而要思考清楚这一点一直都非常困难，

cues.en: because we're so biased by our view and our understanding of modern life. So if we look at modern cells, they're incredibly complicated. Just a lot of moving parts, very elaborate structures, such as you can see here, this elaborate structure in a eukaryotic cell, all the machinery involved in cell division. If you go deeper and look at the underlying biochemistry,
cues.zh: 因为我们对现代生命的认知和理解带来了极大的先入为主的偏见。如果我们观察现代细胞，会发现它们极其复杂。不仅包含大量动态组件，还有非常精细的结构，就像大家在这里看到的，真核细胞中这种精密的结构，以及参与细胞分裂的所有分子机器。如果再进一步深入观察其底层的生化机制，

cues.en: If anything, it's even more complicated. And this is just a small section of the chart of central metabolism. So there are hundreds or thousands of enzymes that catalyze all of the metabolic reactions that are required for cells to grow and divide. Even the general organizational structure of modern cells is very...
cues.zh: 那甚至只会更加复杂。而这仅仅是中心代谢途径图谱的一小部分。有成百上千种酶在催化着细胞生长和分裂所需的所有代谢反应。甚至现代细胞的总体组织结构也是极为……

cues.en: complicated in the sense that it's highly self-referential. So every aspect of this process, the central dogma, the transmission of information from DNA to RNA to proteins, and then down to building structures with function, every part of that depends on all the other parts. So for example, the replication of DNA requires DNA, but it also requires RNA and proteins, the polymerases.
cues.zh: 复杂的，因为它具有高度的自指性。在中心法则这一过程中——信息从 DNA 传递到 RNA 再到蛋白质，进而构建出具有功能的结构——其中的每一个环节都依赖于其他所有环节。比如，DNA 的复制需要 DNA 本身，但它同时也需要 RNA 以及作为聚合酶的蛋白质。

cues.en: The transcription of RNA requires DNA, which is where the information is stored, but it also requires many proteins, and it also requires many other RNA molecules. And similarly, the formation of proteins occurs on a remarkably complex machine, the ribosome, which itself is composed of RNA and proteins. So, for decades, it was very hard for people to think
cues.zh: RNA 的转录需要 DNA（因为信息储存在那里），但它同时也需要很多蛋白质，以及很多其他 RNA 分子。同样，蛋白质的生成发生在极其复杂的机器——核糖体上，而核糖体本身就是由 RNA 和蛋白质组成的。因此，几十年来人们都很难想出

cues.en: of any reasonable way in which such an internally self-referential system could emerge spontaneously from a chemical environment. And the answer to that really came from thinking about RNA and the different things that it can do. So this simplification in thinking came from the realization that RNA can not just carry
cues.zh: 有什么合理的方式，能让这样一个内部自指的系统自发地从化学环境中涌现出来。而这个问题的答案，其实来自对 RNA 及其多种功能的思考。这种思维上的简化，源于人们意识到 RNA 不仅能够携带

cues.en: information, but can also catalyze chemical reactions. And that realization led immediately to the hypothesis that in primitive cells, RNA might be able to catalyze its own replication, also carry out biochemical functions for the primitive cell, and so then all you really need to think about is a cell with RNA molecules encapsulated within some kind of primitive cell membrane.
cues.zh: 信息，还能催化化学反应。这一认知随即催生了一个假说：在原始细胞中，RNA 或许能够催化自身的复制，同时为原始细胞执行生化功能；这样一来，你真正需要考虑的，就只是一个被某种原始细胞膜包裹着 RNA 分子的细胞了。

cues.en: that itself could be a self-replicating structure. So, the history of this idea actually goes back to the 1960s, and three very smart people, Leslie Orgel, Carlos, Francis Crick, hypothesized, in part on the basis of the complex folded structure of tRNA, that an early stage of life might have evolved
cues.zh: 这本身可能是一种自我复制结构。这个想法的历史其实可以追溯到20世纪60年代，三位非常聪明的人——Leslie Orgel、Carlos、Francis Crick——部分基于tRNA复杂的折叠结构推测，生命的早期阶段可能已经演化出

cues.en: RNA as the sole macromolecular basis of evolved machinery. And so this lets you think of simple cells emerging with just a single biopolymer RNA, and then later on, as evolution developed more complex cellular structures,
cues.zh: RNA作为演化机器唯一的大分子基础。这样你就可以想象，简单细胞仅凭一种生物聚合物RNA出现，后来随着演化发展出更复杂的细胞结构，

cues.en: information storage became specialized in DNA, and most functional activities became specialized as the job of proteins. Now, although these ideas were put forth in rather elementary form in the 60s, and of course nobody took them seriously at the time, because there was absolutely no experimental evidence for the idea that RNA could catalyze chemical reactions. At the time, people had
cues.zh: 信息存储专门化到DNA，大多数功能活动则专门化为蛋白质的工作。如今，尽管这些想法在60年代以相当初步的形式提出，当然当时没人当真，因为完全没有实验证据表明RNA能催化化学反应。当时，人们刚

cues.en: just started to get very detailed high-resolution information about how proteins catalyzed reactions. And the idea that a molecule like RNA could do the same thing seemed ludicrous. So it wasn't until almost 20 years later, with the work of Tom Chek and Sid Altman, and the experimental demonstration that RNA molecules could actually...
cues.zh: 刚开始获得关于蛋白质如何催化反应的非常详细的高分辨率信息。而像RNA这样的分子也能做同样的事，这个想法显得荒谬。所以直到近20年后，随着Tom Chek和Sid Altman的工作，以及实验证明RNA分子实际上能够……

cues.en: very effectively catalyzed at least certain types of chemical reactions, that people took this whole idea of an RNA-based early stage of life seriously. And so that hypothesis, the RNA world hypothesis, was really, the ideas were summarized by Wally Gilbert in an article in 1986, and this has really become the foundation of a lot of thinking about
cues.zh: 非常有效地催化至少某些类型的化学反应，人们才开始认真对待这个完整想法：生命早期阶段以RNA为基础。于是这个假说，即RNA世界假说，其思想由Wally Gilbert在1986年的一篇文章中总结，这确实成了许多关于

cues.en: early stages in the emergence of life. Okay, so apart from the basic fact that RNA does and can catalyze chemical reactions, is there any other evidence that early life might have been based more exclusively on nucleic acids? And in fact there are several lines of circumstantial evidence.
cues.zh: 生命出现早期阶段的思考基础。好，那么除了RNA确实且能够催化化学反应这一基本事实之外，还有没有其他证据表明早期生命可能更完全地基于核酸？事实上，有几条间接证据。

cues.en: So, one of them is the structure of many cofactors. So here you see acetyl CoA, just one example. But the working part of the molecule is the thioester out here, and for no obvious reason, there's a nucleotide at the other end. And really the only way to make sense of that is that the nucleotide is a handle.
cues.zh: 其中一条是许多辅因子的结构。这里你看到乙酰辅酶A，只是一个例子。但分子的工作部分是外端的硫酯，而另一端有一个核苷酸，原因并不明显。真正能解释这一点的唯一方式，就是核苷酸是一个“把手”。

cues.en: either a relic of primitive ribosome or something that was easy for primitive ribosomes to grab hold of, and thereby, using this cofactor, catalyzed reactions in a thioester mediated way. Now, there are other examples. Here is vitamin B12, another very important catalyst.
cues.zh: 它要么是原始核糖体的遗物，要么是原始核糖体容易抓住的东西，从而利用这个辅因子，以硫酯介导的方式催化反应。现在还有其他例子。这里是维生素B12，另一种非常重要的催化剂。

cues.en: Its working part is this complex chorin ring, but down here you see again a nucleotide. What's it doing there? It's probably another relic of the RNA world when all of this complicated biochemistry was being catalyzed by RNA enzymes. Yet another example is the very way that the substrates for DNA synthesis are made.
cues.zh: 它的工作部分是这个复杂的咕啉环，但往下这里你又看到一个核苷酸。它在那里做什么？这很可能是RNA世界的另一个遗物，当时所有这些复杂的生化反应都由RNA酶催化。还有一个例子，就是DNA合成底物的制造方式本身。

cues.en: And they're not made de novo, as you might expect if DNA came first. They're actually made from pre-existing ribonucleotides. And so the transformation of ribonucleotides to deoxynucleotides is catalyzed by the enzyme ribonucleotide reductase. And this unusual synthetic pathway can be viewed as the relic of the fact that
cues.zh: 而且它们不是从头合成的，你可能会以为如果 DNA 先出现就会这样。它们实际上由预先存在的核糖核苷酸制成。所以，核糖核苷酸向脱氧核苷酸的转化由核糖核苷酸还原酶催化。这种不寻常的合成途径可以被看作一个遗迹，说明这一事实：

cues.en: Early in time, metabolism and RNA synthesis used ribonucleotides, and only later, when DNA was invented or evolved, was there a requirement to make deoxynucleotides, and so they're made from the closest available substrate. Okay, finally, perhaps the most important and dramatic piece of evidence for the early role of RNA
cues.zh: 在早期，代谢和 RNA 合成使用的是核糖核苷酸，只是后来，当 DNA 被发明或演化出来时，才需要制造脱氧核苷酸，因此它们由现存最接近的底物制成。好，最后，也许关于 RNA 早期作用最重要、最戏剧性的证据

cues.en: in primitive forms of life is the actual structure of the ribosome. And so this is a slide from Tom Steitz showing a view into the active site of the large subunit. So this is the peptidyltransferase center. And this little green structure in here
cues.zh: 在原始生命形态中，就是核糖体的实际结构。这是 Tom Steitz 的一张幻灯片，展示了核糖体大亚基活性位点的视图。这里是肽基转移酶中心。而这里这个小绿色结构

cues.en: is a transition state analog that marks at the place in this gigantic machine where the chemistry is happening. And what you can see is that it's these gray squiggles, which are the RNA, that completely make up that active site. So all proteins...
cues.zh: 是一个过渡态类似物，标记出这台巨大机器中化学反应发生的位置。你能看到，正是这些灰色弯曲线条，也就是 RNA，完全构成了那个活性位点。所以所有蛋白质……

cues.en: are generated by an RNA machine, the RNA central region of the ribosome itself. So again, this only makes sense in terms of an early stage of biochemistry dominated by RNA functions, which then over time evolved the ability to make proteins which are now so important in all modern biochemistry. So, if we want to understand
cues.zh: 都是由 RNA 机器产生的，也就是核糖体自身的 RNA 中央区域。所以再说一次，这只有在由 RNA 功能主导的早期生物化学阶段才说得通；后来随着时间推移，才演化出制造蛋白质的能力，而蛋白质如今在所有现代生物化学中都如此重要。所以，如果我们想理解

cues.en: the origin of life, what we need to think about is not simply how to make these incredibly complex modern cells, but we need to think about how to go from chemistry to very simple RNA-based cellular structures.
cues.zh: 生命的起源，我们需要思考的不只是如何制造这些极其复杂的现代细胞，还需要思考如何从化学走向非常简单的、基于 RNA 的细胞结构。

cues.en: What would the process look like? What's the broader picture? When did this all happen on the early Earth? So what was the timeframe in which these events took place? This is a slide from a review by Jerry Joyce, and it summarizes the broad sweep of events that were important in the origin of life. So we actually need to think of everything from planet formation, the beginning,
cues.zh: 这个过程会是什么样子？更宏观的图景是什么？这一切在早期地球上是什么时候发生的？那么这些事件发生的时间范围是什么？这是 Jerry Joyce 一篇综述中的幻灯片，它概括了生命起源中重要事件的总体脉络。所以我们实际上需要思考从行星形成开始的一切，也就是

cues.en: of the Earth itself around 4.5 billion years ago. Over time, as the Earth cooled, water could condense, we have stable hydrosphere, we have liquid water on the surface. Following that, increasingly complicated organic chemistry going on, probably many different environments on the early planet. And then somehow that led up to the synthesis of RNA or RNA-like molecules.
cues.zh: 地球本身在大约 45 亿年前的开端。随着时间推移，地球冷却，水可以凝结，我们有了稳定的水圈，地表有了液态水。此后，越来越复杂的有机化学持续进行，早期行星上可能有许多不同环境。然后不知怎么地，这促成了 RNA 或类 RNA 分子的合成。

cues.en: on the Earth, which could start to carry out biochemical functions inside primitive cells, and then eventually lead to the emergence of much more complicated cells that would be biochemically similar to modern life. Now, the first really good evidence we have about the appearance of modern microbial life is roughly three and a half billion years ago. So there's a billion year interval between
cues.zh: 在地球上，这些分子可以开始在原始细胞内执行生化功能，然后最终导致复杂得多的细胞出现，而这些细胞在生化上类似于现代生命。现在，我们拥有的关于现代微生物生命出现的第一批真正可靠证据，大约是在 35 亿年前。所以有一个十亿年的间隔，位于

cues.en: the formation and cooling of the planet and the first good evidence for life. And basically, we have very little hard evidence about where all of these important events that led up to life emerging from chemistry, when they actually happened. And that goes along with the fact that we have very little concrete evidence concerning the environments in which those transitions took place. So, this is one of the
cues.zh: 行星的形成和冷却，与最早可靠的生命证据之间。基本上，对于所有这些导致生命从化学中涌现的重要事件究竟发生在哪里、实际发生在什么时候，我们几乎没有硬证据。这也与我们几乎没有具体证据来说明这些转变发生在什么环境中相一致。所以，这是

cues.en: difficult aspects of studying this question. We can't actually go back. We can't know for sure what the early environments were really like. We'll never know exactly what really happened. So what's our goal in studying these questions? What we're trying to do is really come up with a plausibly realistic sequence of events so that we understand all of the transitions throughout this whole pathway.
cues.zh: 研究这个问题最困难的方面之一。我们实际上无法回到过去。我们无法确定早期环境到底是什么样。我们永远无法确切知道真正发生了什么。那么，我们研究这些问题的目标是什么？我们想做的，实际上是提出一个合理可信的事件序列，以便理解整条路径上的所有转变。

cues.en: We'd like to understand a complete pathway from planet formation through early chemistry, more complicated organic chemistry, up to the assembly of those building blocks into the first cells, the emergence of Darwinian evolution, and then the gradual complexification of early life leading up to what we see now. Okay, so let's look a little bit more closely at the chemical steps. So in broad outline, what we think happened
cues.zh: 我们想理解一条完整路径：从行星形成，经过早期化学、更复杂的有机化学，直到把这些构建模块组装成最初的细胞、达尔文演化的出现，再到早期生命逐渐复杂化，一直发展到我们今天看到的样子。好，那我们再仔细看看这些化学步骤。大致来说，我们认为发生的过程是

cues.en: is that you start off with very simple molecules such as shown up here. There's still a lot of debate about the nature of the early atmosphere. Scientific opinions have gone back and forth in terms of the structure and how reducing that atmosphere was. But it's also been recognized that there could be very important local variations. So even if the...
cues.zh: 一开始只有非常简单的小分子，比如上面这些。关于早期大气的性质仍有很多争论。就大气的结构以及它的还原性程度而言，科学界的看法一直反反复复。但人们也认识到，可能存在非常重要的局部差异。所以即使……

cues.en: atmosphere was globally fairly neutral or perhaps mildly reducing or mildly oxidizing. There could be local environments that were more reducing. That, together with the input of various forms of energy, for example from electric discharges, lightning, high energy, ultraviolet radiation, ionizing radiation, these are all forms of very
cues.zh: 大气在全球范围内相当中性，或者可能呈弱还原性或弱氧化性。但仍可能存在还原性更强的局部环境。再加上各种形式能量的输入，比如放电、闪电、高能、紫外线辐射、电离辐射，这些都是非常

cues.en: energetic processes that can basically rip these small starting molecules apart into atoms, which can then recombine to generate high energy intermediates with multiple bonds, molecules like cyanide and acetylene, formaldehyde, and so on.
cues.zh: 高能的过程，基本上能把最初的小分子撕裂成原子，这些原子随后可以重新结合，生成带多重键的高能中间体，比如氰化物、乙炔、甲醛等分子。

cues.en: And these molecules can then start to interact with each other and gradually build up more complex intermediates ultimately leading to the things we really care about. The lipids that will make membranes and vesicles, the nucleotides that will assemble into genetic molecules like RNA.
cues.zh: 然后这些分子开始彼此相互作用，逐渐构建出更复杂的中间体，最终形成我们真正关心的东西。脂质会构成膜和囊泡，核苷酸会组装成 RNA 之类的遗传分子。

cues.en: amino acids that can assemble into peptides, which may also play roles in primitive cells. And somehow, and this is the question that my lab has really been focused on, somehow all of these molecules come together and assemble into larger structures that look and act like cells that can grow and divide. Okay, so how could that possibly happen, and what would such a primitive cell look like?
cues.zh: 氨基酸可以组装成肽，而肽也可能在原始细胞中发挥作用。而且不知怎么地——这正是我们实验室一直重点关注的问题——所有这些分子会聚到一起，组装成更大的结构，看起来像细胞、行为也像细胞，而且能够生长和分裂。好，那这怎么可能发生？这样的原始细胞会是什么样子？

cues.en: And so here is a schematic version of the way that we're thinking about a primitive cell or protocell. So what we think are the important components of a primitive cell are basically two things, a cell membrane, and inside some kind of genetic material. Maybe RNA, maybe DNA, maybe something simpler, something more stable. We're not really sure.
cues.zh: 这里是我们思考原始细胞或原细胞的一种示意图。我们认为原始细胞的重要组分基本上有两样：细胞膜，以及里面某种遗传物质。也许是 RNA，也许是 DNA，也许是更简单、更稳定的东西。我们并不太确定。

cues.en: So the first question is how could you assemble such composite structures? So we want to have a membrane boundary that can keep important molecules encapsulated within and essentially provide a distinction between the cell itself and the rest of the universe. We need to understand how these two components self-assemble, how they come together.
cues.zh: 所以第一个问题是，你如何组装出这样的复合结构？我们希望有一个膜边界，能把重要分子包裹在里面，基本上把细胞本身与宇宙其余部分区分开。我们需要理解这两个组分如何自组装、如何聚到一起。

cues.en: And it actually turns out that that part is all fairly straightforward. Self-assembly processes are critical in thinking about all of these steps, and there are multiple different ways in which these components can be made and can come together. A much harder question and more interesting is, once you have structures like this, how can they grow and then divide?
cues.zh: 事实证明，这部分其实相当简单。在思考所有这些步骤时，自组装过程至关重要，而且这些组分的生成和聚集有许多不同的途径。但更难、也更有趣的问题是：一旦有了这样的结构，它们又该如何生长并分裂？

cues.en: without any of the complicated biochemical machinery that's present in all of modern life. So since we're talking about the origin of life, then by definition we didn't have highly evolved biochemical machinery around. So it's sometimes hard to think about these problems because modern cells use so much biochemical machinery to mediate the process of cell growth and cell division.
cues.zh: 而且不能依赖现代生命中普遍存在的复杂生化机制。既然我们讨论的是生命起源，按定义当时显然还没有高度演化的生化机制。因此思考这些问题有时会很困难，因为现代细胞依赖大量的生化机制来介导细胞生长和分裂的过程。

cues.en: It's almost hard to think of how could that be driven by simple chemical and physical processes. But that's in essence what we need to figure out in order to understand this process. There's no machinery around, so we have to identify the chemical and physical processes that will drive growth and then mediate cell division.
cues.zh: 我们几乎很难想象，这要如何单纯靠简单的物理和化学过程来驱动。但这在本质上正是我们需要弄清楚的，唯有如此才能理解这一过程。当时没有任何现成机制，所以我们必须找出能够驱动生长并介导细胞分裂的物理与化学过程。

cues.en: So that applies not only to the membrane, but also to the genetic material, whether it's RNA or something else. There have to be simple chemical processes that will drive the copying of that information, that will allow the strands to separate so that another round of copying can take place, and that will allow that replicated material to be distributed into daughter cells. So if we can identify
cues.zh: 这不仅适用于细胞膜，也适用于遗传物质，无论它是 RNA 还是其他东西。必须存在简单的化学过程来驱动这些信息的复制，让链条得以分离以便进行下一轮复制，并让复制出的物质分配到子细胞中。所以如果我们能找出……

cues.en: chemical and physical processes that do all of that, we would have a situation where essentially the environment is driving a cycle of growth and division that brings us back to this stage, and you could go around and around that cycle again and again, and that would be just very similar to the way in which modern cells grow and divide. The information within would be...
cues.zh: ……能完成这一切的物理和化学过程，我们就会得到这样一种场景：环境本质上在驱动一个生长与分裂的循环，不断带我们回到起点，你可以一次又一次地循环往复，这已经与现代细胞生长和分裂的方式极其相似。其中的信息也将……

cues.en: propagated and transmitted from generation to generation. And the important thing in terms of the emergence of Darwinian evolution is that during that continuous process of replication, of course mistakes would be made. Over time, more and more of sequence space would be surveyed, and eventually, we think, some sequence would emerge that did something useful for the cell as a whole.
cues.zh: ……代代相传。而对达尔文演化的涌现来说，最关键的是，在持续不断的复制过程中，不可避免地会出现差错。随着时间推移，被探索的序列空间越来越大，我们认为最终会涌现出某种对整个细胞有益的序列。

cues.en: As soon as that happened, that sequence, by conveying an advantage to its own cell, whether in terms of growth rate, or the efficiency of cell division, or the efficiency of survival, it would have an advantage and it would gradually, over generations, take over the population.
cues.zh: 一旦出现这种情况，该序列就会为它所在的细胞带来优势——无论是在生长速度、细胞分裂效率，还是生存能力上——它都将具备竞争优势，并在经过数代演化后，逐渐占据整个群体的主导地位。

cues.en: is really the essence of Darwinian evolution. You have a change in the genetic structure of a population as a result of natural selection. And that is precisely what we would like to see emerge spontaneously in our laboratory experiments. We want to start with a chemical system and watch it transition into the emergence of real Darwinian evolution at a very simple level.
cues.zh: 这正是达尔文进化论的精髓。种群遗传结构因自然选择而发生改变。而这正是我们希望在实验室实验中自发涌现的现象。我们想从一个化学系统开始，观察它如何转变，在非常简单的层面上涌现出真正的达尔文进化。

cues.en: Okay, so let's step back again and think about how all of these molecules would be made in the environment of a primitive planet. And of course the first breakthrough in this research program was the famous Miller-Urey experiment, in which a mixture of reducing gases was subjected to an electric spark discharge and the products were analyzed. And amazingly, in that...
cues.zh: 好，我们再退一步，想想这些分子在原始行星环境中会如何形成。当然，这个研究计划的第一个突破就是著名的 Miller-Urey 实验：将还原性气体混合物经受电火花放电，然后分析产物。而令人惊讶的是，在那次……

cues.en: a different mix of products were many of the amino acids, which are major components of the proteins of modern cells. So that was really a revelation. It really took people by surprise that the building blocks of biological structures could be generated in such an easy manner. Now, in fact, that result was so powerful that it...
cues.zh: 在不同产物混合物中，有许多氨基酸，而它们是现代细胞蛋白质的主要成分。所以那真是一个重大启示。生物结构的构建单元竟能如此轻易地生成，这确实让人吃惊。事实上，那个结果如此有力，以至于它……

cues.en: might have actually been a little bit distracting. Probably the really important thing that's made in this kind of experiment is not amino acids per se, but high energy intermediates like cyanide and acetylene. Those are the kinds of molecules that can assemble in subsequent steps into nucleotides, the building blocks of genetic materials.
cues.zh: 可能实际上有点让人分心。也许这类实验真正重要的产物并不是氨基酸本身，而是像氰化物和乙炔这样的高能中间体。这类分子可以在后续步骤中组装成核苷酸，也就是遗传物质的构建单元。

cues.en: Well, so those molecules are thought to have been made in primitive environments, so that was an electric discharge experiment, which is very analogous to the kinds of lightning displays that you get in volcanic scenarios. So this is the lightning that's going on in the ash cloud of a currently erupting volcano in southern Chile.
cues.zh: 嗯，所以人们认为这些分子是在原始环境中形成的；那是一个放电实验，与火山场景中出现的各种闪电现象非常类似。这就是智利南部一座正在喷发的火山灰云中发生的闪电。

cues.en: So, since the early Earth was thought to be highly volcanically active, this seems like a very reasonable scenario. Okay, but what about some of the other molecules that we need to build our primitive early cell? We need to have lipid-like molecules, amphiphilic molecules, that can self-assemble into membranes and generate compartments spontaneously. So, these are molecules that are amphiphilic.
cues.zh: 那么，由于早期地球被认为火山活动非常活跃，这似乎是一个非常合理的场景。好，但我们需要用来构建原始早期细胞的其他一些分子呢？我们需要类脂分子，也就是两亲性分子，它们能自组装成膜并自发形成区室。所以，这些就是两亲性分子。

cues.en: They have one part that likes to be in water and another part that doesn't like to be in water. And the way that those preferences are balanced is by forming membranes in which the non-polar parts are on the inside and the polar parts of the molecules face out into the water. So it turns out that it's actually, again, very easy to make molecules like that in a variety of different scenarios. In fact,
cues.zh: 它们有一部分喜欢待在水里，另一部分不喜欢待在水里。平衡这些倾向的方式，就是形成膜，其中非极性部分在内侧，分子的极性部分朝外面向水。所以事实证明，在各种不同场景中，制造这类分子其实又非常容易。事实上，

cues.en: Dave Diemer and his colleagues showed that you can extract molecules from the Murchison meteorite. It's one of these carbonaceous chondrite meteorites that's rich in organic materials. You can extract molecules that will self-assemble into vesicles, as you can see here. So they spontaneously make membrane sheets that close up into small vesicles. Here's another example. This is an experiment that was done to
cues.zh: Dave Diemer 和他的同事表明，可以从 Murchison 陨石中提取分子。它是富含有机物质的碳质球粒陨石之一。你可以提取出能自组装成囊泡的分子，正如你在这里看到的。所以它们会自发形成膜片，并闭合成为小囊泡。这里还有一个例子。这是一个实验，目的是……

cues.en: mimic processes going on in interstellar molecular clouds where you have various gases that have condensed on the surface of solica particles. They're subjected to irradiation by ultraviolet light and ionizing radiation. So if you make ices like that in the laboratory, subject them to ultraviolet radiation, you get a lot of complicated chemistry going on.
cues.zh: 模拟星际分子云中发生的过程，在那里各种气体凝结在二氧化硅颗粒表面。它们受到紫外光和电离辐射的照射。所以，如果在实验室中制造这样的冰，并让它们接受紫外线辐射，就会发生大量复杂的化学反应。

cues.en: And then in that vast mix of products, you can extract molecules, which again will form membranes and self-assemble into these vesicle compartments. Here is yet another scenario. This is a hydrothermal synthesis done by Bob Hazen and Dave Diemer. Again, in hydrothermal processing, you can grow carbon chains with...
cues.zh: 在那些庞杂的产物混合物中，你可以提取出能形成膜并自组装成囊泡隔室的分子。这里还有另一种可能的情景，这是 Bob Hazen 和 Dave Diemer 完成的水热合成实验。同样地，在水热反应中，你能合成出带有……的碳链，

cues.en: oxygenated groups such as carboxylates at the end, and these self-assemble into membranes and make many compartments, as you can see in this beautiful image. Okay, so what would be an example of an early Earth environment where something like this could take place? There are a series of experiments from the Siminate lab that suggest that hydrothermal synthesis could happen
cues.zh: 末端带有羧酸基等含氧基团，它们会自组装成膜，形成许多隔室，正如这幅绝美图像所示。好，那么早期地球上，什么环境下可能发生这种过程呢？Siminate 实验室的一系列实验表明，水热合成可能发生于……

cues.en: deep down in regions with high temperature and high pressure on the surface of catalytic minerals such as transition metal, sulfides, or oxides. And those reactions would basically turn hydrogen and carbon monoxide into fatty acids and related compounds.
cues.zh: 地下深处的高温高压区域，在过渡金属硫化物或氧化物等催化性矿物的表面发生。这些反应基本上能将氢气和一氧化碳转化为脂肪酸及相关化合物。

cues.en: Next slide here is a movie that was prepared by Janet Iwasa that illustrates this process. So we're going deep into the Earth, down through the water channels of a geyser, and here we're looking at the surface of these catalytic transition metal minerals.
cues.zh: 下一页幻灯片是 Janet Iwasa 制作的动画，生动展示了这一过程。我们深入地底，穿过间歇泉的水流通道，在这里我们能看到这些起催化作用的过渡金属矿物表面。

cues.en: and you can see hydrogen and carbon monoxide molecules bouncing around the surface, and the mineral is catalyzing their assembly into chains, which eventually will be released and float up, and they'll be caught up in the flow of water and thereby brought to the surface, where you can imagine these fatty acids, fatty alcohols, and related molecules
cues.zh: 可以看到氢气和一氧化碳分子在表面碰撞弹跳，矿物催化它们组装成链，这些分子链最终脱离并向上漂浮，被水流裹挟着带到地表，你可以想象这些脂肪酸、脂肪醇和相关分子……

cues.en: being aerosolized and concentrated in droplets, and perhaps even building up into large deposits on the land surface. So it doesn't seem like the prebiotic assembly of molecules that could spontaneously form membrane vesicles is all that difficult. It's definitely an understudied area of prebiotic chemistry. It needs more work, but it looks, I think, reasonably plausible.
cues.zh: 被气溶胶化并在液滴中浓缩，甚至可能在陆地表面形成大量沉积物。所以，能自发形成膜囊泡的分子的前生命期组装，看起来并没有那么困难。这绝对是前生命化学中研究不足的一个领域，需要更多探索，但我认为它非常合情合理。

cues.en: So the most prebiotically likely molecules would be things like capric acid that you see down here, short chain saturated fatty acids. So we do experiments in the lab with molecules like this, but we also use longer chain unsaturated molecules like myristoliac acid and oleic acid as model systems because they're just generally easier to work with.
cues.zh: 因此，生命起源前最可能存在的分子，就是大家在下方看到的癸酸这类短链饱和脂肪酸。我们在实验室中会用这类分子做实验，但也会用肉豆蔻油酸和油酸这类长链不饱和分子作为模型系统，因为它们通常更容易操作。

cues.en: So, what happens if you just take one of these fatty acids and shake it up in water with some salt and buffer? Is it hard to make membranes? No. What you can see is that you just spontaneously...
cues.zh: 那么，如果你取其中一种脂肪酸，加点盐和缓冲液在水中摇晃，会发生什么？形成膜很困难吗？不难。你会看到它直接自发地……

cues.en: make vesicles in a huge variety of complex structures, a huge range of sizes, all the way from 30 microns, this large vesicle, to many, many smaller vesicles ranging down to 30 nanometers. Many of these vesicles are composed of multiple sheets of membrane.
cues.zh: 形成结构极为多样复杂、尺寸跨度极大的囊泡，从这个大到 30 微米的大囊泡，到许多小至 30 纳米的极小囊泡。其中许多囊泡都是由多层膜片构成的。

cues.en: So stacks of membranes. You can see some of these vesicles have smaller vesicles inside them. So it's a very heterogeneous, complex mixture. Now, the other thing that's really important about this is that these vesicles, these membranes have very, very different properties from modern biological membranes. Modern membranes are basically, they've evolved to be good barriers.
cues.zh: 所以是一层层的膜堆叠。你能看到有些囊泡里面还有更小的囊泡。所以这是非常异质、复杂的混合物。另一件很重要的事是，这些囊泡、这些膜的性质与现代生物膜非常非常不同。现代膜基本上已经进化成很好的屏障。

cues.en: so that cells can control the flow of all molecules in and out using complicated protein machines. For a primitive cell, you wouldn't want a situation like that. That would be suicidal. These molecules have to let stuff get across. They have to have dynamic properties that can let them grow and equilibrate.
cues.zh: 这样细胞就能用复杂的蛋白质机器控制所有分子进出。对原始细胞来说，你并不想要那种情况。那等于自杀。这些分子必须让物质穿过去。它们必须具有动态性质，能让膜生长并达到平衡。

cues.en: Okay, so the next slide is actually a movie, again prepared by Janet Iwasa, to illustrate the dynamic properties of these vesicles, which are so different from modern membranes. And so what you can see here is, first of all, the motion on the surface, a lot of oscillations, diffusion. In the membrane itself...
cues.zh: 好，下一张幻灯片其实是一段动画，同样由 Janet Iwasa 制作，用来展示这些囊泡的动态性质，它们与现代膜如此不同。这里你能看到，首先是表面上的运动，大量振荡、扩散。在膜本身内部……

cues.en: These molecules, the individual molecules, are rapidly flip-flopping back and forth from inside to outside. They're constantly entering the membrane, leaving the membrane. So there's a lot of exchange reactions that are going on on very rapid timescales on the order of a second or less. So they're very dynamic structures.
cues.zh: 这些分子，单个分子，在内外之间快速来回翻转。它们不断进入膜、离开膜。所以有大量交换反应在非常快的时间尺度上进行，大约一秒或更短。所以它们是非常动态的结构。

cues.en: And these dynamic motions are also probably very important in terms of permeability. They allow the formation of transient defects in the membrane which let molecules get across spontaneously without any complicated machinery. There's another property of these vesicles which I find quite fascinating. So, as you saw in the illustration, the molecules that make up any given vesicle
cues.zh: 这些动态运动很可能对通透性也很重要。它们让膜中形成瞬时缺陷，使分子无需任何复杂机器就能自发穿过。这些囊泡还有一个我觉得相当迷人的性质。正如你在图示中看到的，构成任意一个囊泡的分子

cues.en: come and go and therefore exchange between vesicles on the time scale of roughly a second. In this slide what you see are two populations of vesicles that were labeled with phospholipid dyes, so they're not exchanging between vesicles. The picture here was taken after about a day.
cues.zh: 会来来去去，因此在约一秒的时间尺度上在囊泡之间交换。这张幻灯片中，你看到的是两组用磷脂染料标记的囊泡，所以它们不会在囊泡之间交换。这里的照片是在大约一天后拍摄的。

cues.en: And so you can see that they haven't all just fused and mixed up. There are still red vesicles and green vesicles. And yet we know from our other experiments that the molecules that make up any one of these vesicles are changing on a very rapid time scale. Yet the structures themselves maintain their identity on a time scale of weeks or months.
cues.zh: 所以你能看到，它们并没有全部融合混在一起。仍然有红色囊泡和绿色囊泡。但我们从其他实验知道，构成任意一个囊泡的分子都在非常快的时间尺度上变化。然而这些结构本身能在数周或数月的时间尺度上保持自身特性。

cues.en: Okay, what about the nucleic acids then? We've talked a lot about the building blocks of membranes, the way they self-assemble, and the properties of the membranes that they assemble into. Let's go back to the genetic materials and think about what kinds of building blocks we need to assemble molecules like RNA. Now, again, we have a difference between the molecules used in modern life. So these, of course, are nucleoside triphosphates.
cues.zh: 好，那核酸呢？我们已经讲了很多膜的构建单元、它们自组装的方式，以及它们组装成的膜的性质。让我们回到遗传物质，想想需要什么样的构建单元来组装 RNA 这样的分子。现在，同样，现代生命所用的分子有所不同。当然，这些就是核苷三磷酸。

cues.en: They're almost ideal substrates for a highly evolved cell with very, very powerful catalysts. These molecules are kinetically trapped in a high-energy state.
cues.zh: 对于拥有极其强大催化剂的高度进化细胞来说，它们几乎是理想的底物。这些分子在动力学上被困在高能状态。

cues.en: They don't spontaneously react very well at all, so it takes a very sophisticated catalyst to use molecules like this as a substrate. They're also, of course, very polar. The triphosphate group is highly charged, and that prevents these molecules from leaking out of the cell, which would be a bad thing. On the other hand, in a primitive cell,
cues.zh: 它们基本不会自发反应，所以需要非常复杂的催化剂才能将这类分子用作底物。当然，它们的极性也很强。三磷酸基团带有大量电荷，能防止这些分子从细胞中泄漏出去——泄漏显然是坏事。而在原始细胞中，

cues.en: If you imagine that substrates, food molecules, are being made in chemical processes out in the environment, it needs to be possible for those molecules to get across the membrane spontaneously and get into the interior of the cell. So then we need to think about different kinds of substrates, molecules that are less polar, so they can get into the cell, and more chemically reactive, so that they can polymerize
cues.zh: 如果你设想底物，也就是养分分子，是在外部环境的化学过程中生成的，那么这些分子必须能够自发穿过细胞膜进入细胞内部。因此我们就得考虑不同类型的底物：极性更弱，以便进入细胞；化学活性更强，以便发生聚合反应——

cues.en: without the need for very sophisticated, advanced, highly evolved catalysts. And so molecules like this were first made by Leslie Orgel and his students and colleagues 20 to 30 years ago and studied in quite a bit of detail as models for the early replication of RNA.
cues.zh: ——而不需要非常复杂、高级且高度进化的催化剂。这类分子最早是由 Leslie Orgel 和他的学生及同事在二三十年前合成的，并作为早期 RNA 复制的模型进行了相当详细的研究。

cues.en: This brings us back to the question of what was the first genetic material? Was it RNA in fact? Or is RNA so complicated or its building blocks so hard to make that life more likely began with something simpler, something easier to make, maybe something more stable that could accumulate like DNA for example?
cues.zh: 这就让我们回到了这个问题：第一种遗传物质究竟是什么？真的是 RNA 吗？还是说 RNA 过于复杂、或者它的构件太难制造，以至于生命更可能始于某种更简单、更容易生成、也许更稳定且能积累的物质，比如 DNA？

cues.en: So this is an area of active debate and investigation. We really don't know the answer to this question, but lots of people are doing experiments and trying to work out chemical pathways leading up to RNA. For example, the Sutherland lab in the UK has made a lot of progress in this area. We're studying...
cues.zh: 所以这是一个充满热烈争论与探索的领域。我们确实还不知道答案，但许多人正在做实验，试图找出生成 RNA 的化学路径。例如，英国的 Sutherland 实验室在这方面取得了很大进展。而我们正在研究的是……

cues.en: how these molecules could be assembled and replicated. So one of the satisfying things about thinking about RNA as the first genetic material is that we actually have two different chemical-physical processes that can lead to the polymerization of activated building blocks into long RNA chains. The first of these was discovered by Jim Ferris, working with Leslie Orgel.
cues.zh: ……这些分子是如何组装和复制的。把 RNA 视为第一种遗传物质，让人欣慰的一点在于，我们其实有两种不同的物理化学过程，可以促使活化的构件聚合成 RNA 长链。其中第一种是由 Jim Ferris 与 Leslie Orgel 合作发现的。

cues.en: And that was the discovery that a common clay mineral, known as montmorillonite, can catalyze the assembly of nucleotides into RNA chains. So this illustrates the structure of this clay. It's a layered hydroxide mineral. In between the layer, the silicate, alumina silicate layers, there's water. And in these interlayers, organic molecules can accumulate
cues.zh: 他们发现一种常见的黏土矿物——蒙脱石，能够催化核苷酸组装成 RNA 链。这里展示的就是这种黏土的结构。它是一种层状氢氧化物矿物。在硅酸盐、铝硅酸盐层之间存在水分。在这些层间，有机分子可以不断积累，

cues.en: And when they're brought close together, they can react with each other and start to polymerize. Okay, so here is some of the experimental data. So, over a period of days, you start off with small chains, and then gradually they get longer and longer, up to lengths of roughly 40, and in more recent experiments, up to 50 or 60 nucleotides long. Okay, so I wanted to illustrate that with this movie, another one of Janet Iwasa's animations.
cues.zh: 当它们彼此靠得很近时，就会发生反应并开始聚合。好，这里展示的是一些实验数据。在几天的时间里，起初是短链，随后逐渐变长，长度大约达到 40 个，而在最近的实验中，已经可以达到 50 到 60 个核苷酸长。好的，我想用这段视频来说明这一点，这也是 Janet Iwasa 制作的另一段动画。

cues.en: to show roughly how we think this works. So these chemically activated building blocks like to stick to the surface of the clay mineral, and when they stick in such a way that they're lined up with each other, they can react and assemble a chemically linked backbone, as you see here. Okay.
cues.zh: 大致说明一下我们认为这是怎么发生的。这些化学活化的构件喜欢附着在黏土矿物表面，当它们以彼此对齐的方式附着时，就能发生反应，组装出化学连接的骨架，如你在这里所见。好。

cues.en: Now, there is another process that can do the same thing, which is very interesting because it's so counter-intuitive. It turns out if you take these same building blocks and just have them in a dilute solution and put that on your bench, nothing happens. But if you take that same solution and put it in the freezer and then come back the next day, you'll find RNA chains. Why is that? It's because when water freezes and forms ice crystals,
cues.zh: 现在，还有另一种过程也能做到同样的事，这很有意思，因为它非常反直觉。事实证明，如果你把这些同样的构件放在稀溶液中，再放到实验台上，什么也不会发生。但如果你把同样的溶液放进冷冻室，第二天再回来，就会发现 RNA 链。为什么呢？这是因为当水结冰并形成冰晶时，

cues.en: that during the growth of the ice crystals, other molecules, solutes, are excluded from the growing crystal. And so they end up concentrated as much as a thousand-fold.
cues.zh: 在冰晶生长过程中，其他分子，也就是溶质，会被排除在正在生长的晶体之外。于是它们最终会被浓缩，浓度可提高多达一千倍。

cues.en: in between the grains of ice. And so when they're so concentrated, again, they can react and polymerize. So having two different processes that can lead to the assembly of RNA chains is actually a very satisfying thing. It's something we look for in this field. If there's more than one way of solving a problem, it makes the whole solution seem more robust. Okay. Now, the hardest problem, perhaps, is once you've got RNA chains like this,
cues.zh: 就在冰粒之间。所以当它们浓度这么高时，又能发生反应并聚合。因此，有两种不同过程都能导致 RNA 链的组装，这其实非常令人满意。这正是我们在这一领域所寻找的。如果解决一个问题有不止一种方法，整个解决方案就会显得更稳健。好。那么，也许最难的问题是，一旦你得到了这样的 RNA 链，

cues.en: How can they be replicated? So much of our early thinking was based on RNA catalysis, and in fact the whole basis of the RNA world is the idea that RNA can act as an enzyme that could catalyze its own replication. And Dave Bartel, when he was a student in my lab many years ago, actually evolved an RNA enzyme with a catalytic activity that can ligate together
cues.zh: 它们如何被复制？我们早期很多思考都基于 RNA 催化，而事实上，RNA 世界的基础就是：RNA 可以作为酶，催化自身的复制。Dave Bartel 很多年前在我实验室做学生时，实际上进化出了一种 RNA 酶，其催化活性可以把

cues.en: pieces of RNA. And Dave subsequently evolved this ribosome into an even more complex structure that is really an RNA polymerase made out of RNA. Now, that's a very impressive proof of principle, but unfortunately, despite many advances over the years, we're still far from having an RNA molecule that can completely catalyze the copying of its own sequence.
cues.zh: RNA 片段连接起来。Dave 随后又把这种核酶进化成更复杂的结构，实际上就是由 RNA 构成的 RNA 聚合酶。现在，这是非常令人印象深刻的原理验证，但不幸的是，尽管多年来有很多进展，我们仍然远未得到一种能完全催化自身序列复制的 RNA 分子。

cues.en: What we've decided to do is to actually, again, step back and try to look at the underlying chemistry and see if there might be ways of adjusting or playing with the chemistry of RNA polymerization that would simplify this problem. Ideally, perhaps we will be able to find a complete chemical process that could drive RNA replication.
cues.zh: 我们决定做的，其实是再次退一步，试着审视底层化学，看看是否有办法调整或摆弄 RNA 聚合的化学过程，从而简化这个问题。理想情况下，也许我们能找到一种完整的化学过程来驱动 RNA 复制。

cues.en: Now, that's a very difficult task. Leslie Orgel and his colleagues worked on that for many years, got partway to a solution, but were never able to have complete cycles of replication. But we have decided to go back and look at some model systems and see if we can get some clues as to how to approach that problem.
cues.zh: 现在，这是一项非常困难的任务。Leslie Orgel 和他的同事为此工作了很多年，取得了一部分进展，但始终无法实现完整的复制循环。但我们决定回过头去研究一些模型系统，看看能否获得一些线索，知道该如何着手解决这个问题。

cues.en: perhaps in some fresh ways. So, just to illustrate what we're really after, I want to show another of Janet Iwasa's movies, and so what you see here is an RNA template, a single-stranded molecule, floating in a solution full of activated monomers, which then find their complementary bases, so they use Watson-Crick base pairing to line up on the template, and then they basically click together to build up a complementary...
cues.zh: 也许能有一些全新的方式。为了说明我们究竟在追求什么，我想展示一段 Janet Iwasa 制作的动画，大家在这里看到的是一条 RNA 模板链，也就是一个单链分子，漂浮在充满活化单体的溶液中，单体找到互补碱基，利用沃森-克里克碱基配对在模板上排列开来，然后基本就像拼积木一样拼接在一起，构建出互补的……

cues.en: strand, generating a duplex product. So, we're after some kind of simple chemical system that would drive that process very efficiently. So, if we could get to that point, then we would be back to being able to assemble this kind of model system, a model protocell, composed of a membrane compartment boundary,
cues.zh: 新链，从而生成双链产物。因此，我们想要的是某种简单的化学系统，能够极高效地驱动这一过程。如果能做到这一点，我们就能回过头来组装出这种模型系统——一个由膜区室边界构成的原始细胞模型，

cues.en: and replicating genetic material on the inside. Now, when we're thinking of a complex composite system like this, the question often arises as to why really bother with the membrane compartment? Why not just let the RNA molecules replicate in solution? And one way of thinking about that is that for Darwinian evolution to emerge,
cues.zh: 内部则包含自我复制的遗传物质。现在，当我们思考这样一个复杂的复合系统时，往往会产生一个疑问：为什么一定要费事弄个膜区室呢？为什么不直接让 RNA 分子在溶液里复制？一种思考方式是，达尔文式进化要想出现，

cues.en: molecules that are in some way better than their neighbors have to have an advantage for themselves. So if we think about RNA replicas floating around in solution, so these would be RNA molecules that catalyze the replication of another RNA molecule, it doesn't really help if you have a mutation which is faster or more accurate if all it's doing is copying random other RNAs that it bumps into
cues.zh: 某些在某方面优于邻居的分子，就必须能为自身带来优势。如果我们设想在溶液中游荡的 RNA 复制催化分子——也就是催化另一个 RNA 分子复制的 RNA——就算突变产生了一个复制速度更快或更精确的分子，但如果它复制的只是在溶液里随机撞到的其他 RNA，

cues.en: in solution. It has to have an advantage for itself. And the simplest way to imagine that happening is to encapsulate these molecules within a vesicle so that they're always copying molecules that are related by descent. Now, the self-assembly of these kinds of complex structures is something that's actually quite simple. So at the lowest...
cues.zh: 那其实没有任何意义。它必须能给自身带来优势。而最简单的实现方式，就是将这些分子包裹在囊泡中，使它们始终在复制具有亲缘关系的分子。其实，这类复杂结构的自组装过程相当简单。在最基本的……

cues.en: level, the formation of a membrane vesicle can just encapsulate whatever is there in the surrounding solution. However, it's intriguing that there are ways of making the process more efficient, and one of the most interesting ways of doing that is to take advantage of that same clay mineral, Montmorillonite, that we've already seen can catalyze the assembly of RNA strands. And so what you can see in this picture
cues.zh: 层面上，膜囊泡的形成可以直接包裹住周围溶液中的任何物质。然而有趣的是，我们有办法让这个过程更高效，其中最巧妙的方法之一，就是利用同一种黏土矿物——蒙脱石，正如我们前面见过的，它能催化 RNA 链的组装。大家在这张图片中可以看到，

cues.en: which was generated by Shelly Fujikawa and Marty Henchak when they were in my lab about eight years ago. What you can see is that we have here a clay particle which has RNA molecules bound to its surface, so the orange color is a dilated RNA. And it turns out these clay particles can catalyze the assembly of membrane sheets
cues.zh: 这张图是大约八年前 Shelly Fujikawa 和 Marty Henchak 在我实验室时制作的。可以看到，这里有一个黏土颗粒，表面结合了 RNA 分子，橙色部分就是标记的 RNA。事实证明，这些黏土颗粒能够催化脂肪酸

cues.en: from fatty acids. And what's happened here is that this clay particle has catalyzed the assembly of this large surrounding vesicle, as well as the many smaller vesicles encapsulated within. So, what we now can see is that a single, very common abundant mineral can catalyze the assembly of a genetic material. It can catalyze the assembly of compartment boundaries, cell membranes.
cues.zh: 组装成膜层。这里发生的是，黏土颗粒催化组装出了外围这个巨大的囊泡，以及内部包裹的许多微小囊泡。因此，我们现在看到，一种非常常见且储量丰富的单一矿物，既能催化遗传物质的组装，又能催化区室边界——也就是细胞膜的组装。

cues.en: and it can help bring them together. So, very intriguing as a way of simplifying the assembly of cell-like structures on the early Earth. Here's another picture, a clay particle inside a vesicle. Here, the boundary is quite dramatically evident, so this is a stack of many layers of membrane bilayers.
cues.zh: 并且它有助于把它们聚合起来。所以，作为简化早期地球类细胞结构组装的一种方式，这非常引人入胜。这是另一张图：囊泡内的一个黏土颗粒。这里边界非常明显，这是许多层膜双层堆叠而成的。

cues.en: Here's yet another example where the large outer vesicle is filled with hundreds of smaller vesicles all assembled under the catalytic influence of this clay particle in the middle. So, assembling these things looks fairly simple. What about the process of growth and division? After all, that's what we really need to generate cell-like structures that can propagate.
cues.zh: 还有一个例子：大的外层囊泡里充满数百个更小的囊泡，它们都是在中间这个黏土颗粒的催化作用下组装起来的。所以，组装这些东西看起来相当简单。那么生长和分裂的过程呢？毕竟，我们真正需要的就是这个过程，来生成能够增殖的类细胞结构。

cues.en: At this point, what I can say is that we've come up with a process that looks fairly robust. We can start with vesicles, add food in the form of fatty acid micelles. They grow remarkably into filamentous structures, which can then divide very easily into daughter cells. And this generates a cycle that can go around and around indefinitely.
cues.zh: 目前我能说的是，我们提出了一个看起来相当稳健的过程。我们可以从囊泡开始，以脂肪酸胶束的形式加入“食物”。它们会显著生长成丝状结构，然后很容易分裂成子细胞。这就产生了一个可以无限循环往复的周期。

cues.en: And in the next part of this lecture, I'll go into much more detail about the nature of this process and the mechanism by which this happens. But, putting this cycle together with our thinking about nucleic acid replication, we can actually start to imagine what a primitive cell cycle would have looked like.
cues.zh: 在本讲座的下一部分，我会更详细地讲这个过程的性质及其发生机制。但是，把这个周期与我们对核酸复制的思考结合起来，我们其实就可以开始想象原始细胞周期会是什么样子。

cues.en: And so this is shown in this figure from a Scientific American article that I wrote with Alonso Ricardo from my lab. And it summarizes some of our ideas about the ways in which the early Earth environment might help to drive cell growth and division. So the idea is that the general environment should be rather cold, perhaps even an ice-covered pond,
cues.zh: 这一点展示在这张图里，它来自我和实验室的 Alonso Ricardo 合写的一篇 Scientific American 文章。它总结了我们的一些想法：早期地球环境可能如何帮助驱动细胞生长和分裂。所以思路是，总体环境应该相当冷，甚至可能是一个冰封的池塘，

cues.en: something you might find in an Arctic or an Alpine environment. There are many examples on the modern Earth. The reason for wanting a cold environment in general is that the copying chemistry seems to go better.
cues.zh: 这种环境你可能在北极或高山环境中见到。现代地球上有很多例子。总的来说，想要冷环境的原因是复制化学似乎进行得更好。

cues.en: at low temperatures. The low temperature helps the building blocks to bind to the template and facilitates the copying process. But then we know that eventually, once copying is complete, you have to get the strands apart so that you can undergo another round of copying. The simplest way for that to happen is to invoke high temperatures. And so what we like to think about are convection cells driven by geothermal energy. So essentially in a hot spring type of environment,
cues.zh: 在低温下。低温有助于构建单元与模板结合，并促进复制过程。但我们也知道，最终一旦复制完成，必须把链分开，才能进行下一轮复制。最简单的办法就是借助高温。所以我们喜欢设想的是由地热能驱动的对流胞。所以本质上，在温泉类环境中，

cues.en: that you could have a pond that's mostly cold, but every now and then these particles would get caught up in a plume of hot water rising from a hot spring. They'd be transiently exposed to high temperatures that would result in strand separation. It also allows for a rapid influx of nutrients from the environment to feed growth and replication through the next round.
cues.zh: 你可以有一个大部分是冷的池塘，但时不时这些颗粒会被卷入从温泉上升的热水羽流中。它们会短暂暴露在高温下，从而导致链分离。这也让环境中的营养物质快速涌入，为下一轮生长和复制提供养分。

cues.en: And then that would generate a cycle in which the entire process of growth and replication and division is driven by fluctuations in the environment. This is driving us to talk to geologists and to search for analogs of this kind of environment on the modern Earth.
cues.zh: 这样就会形成一个循环，整个生长、复制和分裂的过程都由环境波动驱动。这也促使我们与地质学家交流，并在现代地球上寻找类似的环境模型。

cues.en: Here is a beautiful image of an Antarctic lake, in which you see stromatolites. These mounds here are microbial growths on the surface. And the reason that it's liquid is that, of course, there is heat rising up from below, geothermally. So it's not a perfect analog of the scenario I described. We would like to find environments like this, where there are hot springs generating convection cells that could drive the whole cycle.
cues.zh: 这是一张南极湖泊的壮丽图像，里面可以看到叠层石。这些土丘是表面生长的微生物堆积物。而它之所以呈液态，自然是因为来自地下的地热上升。所以它并不是我所描述场景的完美对应物。我们希望能找到这类环境，通过温泉产生对流胞，从而驱动整个循环。

cues.en: So that would be very satisfying if we could identify such environments. Okay, so what I've tried to show in this lecture is basically the context of the environment and the chemistry leading up to the assembly of primitive cells in a way that's plausible on the early Earth.
cues.zh: 如果我们真能找到这样的环境，那就太令人振奋了。好的，本讲我想向大家展示的，基本就是在早期地球合理条件下，促成原始细胞组装的环境背景与化学过程。
